correctness.rationale: The motivating paper explicitly declares the Caputo-Fabrizio operator and later writes its Losada-Nieto integral as a local term plus an ordinary integral. Applying that exact relation to the paper's scalar total-rodent equation yields the stated compatibility condition and exponential positive-time transient. The paper's Mittag-Leffler expression is instead the classical Caputo solution. The cited Diethelm-Ford-Freed method explicitly defines the classical Caputo operator and derives power-law Volterra history weights, matching the structure printed in the motivating numerical section. The bundled checker independently verifies the scalar CF integral identity and compatibility formula.

value.rationale: The paper's principal fractional-order interpretation is based on varying the memory order and reading changes in epidemic peaks and equilibria. Caputo and Caputo-Fabrizio operators have different memory kernels and different scalar resolvents, so using the former's predictor-corrector for the latter changes the mathematical model being simulated rather than merely changing a coefficient. The finding gives an exact scalar diagnostic and identifies which integer-order conclusions remain unaffected.
